questions.say: Good morning. My name is Daniel, and I'm your examiner today. This is the Speaking test. In this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about your hometown. Where is your hometown?

questions.text: What is the best way to travel around your hometown?

cueCard.topic: Describe a street you like in your town or city.
cueCard.explain: and explain why you like this street.

questions.text: Describe a street you like in your town or city.
questions.say: Thank you. Now, in Part 2, I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here is your topic. Describe a street you like in your town or city. You should say: where it is; what you can see there; how often you go there; and explain why you like this street.

questions.text: Is this street busy at the weekend?
questions.say: Thank you. Is this street busy at the weekend?

questions.text: What makes a street a pleasant place to walk along?
questions.say: Thank you. We've been talking about a street you like in your town or city, and I'd like to discuss with you some more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all streets and neighbourhoods. What makes a street a pleasant place to walk along?

questions.text: Should some city streets be closed to cars?

questions.text: Why do some neighbourhoods become more popular than others?

questions.text: What should town planners think about when they design a new area?

questions.text: Is it better to repair old buildings or to build new ones?
